active_papers.source_text: AGN hosts exhibit a measurable star-formation deficit relative to inactive galaxies matched in stellar mass, morphology, halo environment, and redshift only when the feedback energy budget can couple to the molecular or ionized gas reservoir.
active_papers.title: Observational constraints on the suppression of star formation by AGN feedback

active_papers.source_text: Environmental quenching contributes an excess quenched fraction at fixed stellar mass below a halo- and redshift-dependent transition, whereas internal/AGN-linked channels dominate at higher stellar or halo mass.
active_papers.title: Separating internal and environmental quenching across stellar mass, halo mass, and redshift

active_papers.source_text: For massive central galaxies and groups, the time-averaged mechanical power from radio-mode AGN balances hot-halo cooling often enough to maintain low star-formation rates.
active_papers.title: Empirical duty-cycle constraints on AGN maintenance heating in massive halos

active_papers.source_text: A substantial fraction of AGN-driven outflowing gas remains gravitationally bound and recycles through the circumgalactic medium, limiting the permanence of feedback-driven gas removal.
active_papers.title: Escape versus recycling: the fate of AGN-driven multiphase outflows

active_papers.source_text: The fraction of radio-jet mechanical power deposited into the multiphase interstellar or circumgalactic medium varies systematically with ambient gas density and host environment.
active_papers.title: Environmental dependence of radio-jet coupling efficiency in galaxy gas

active_papers.source_text: There is a stellar/halo-mass regime where stellar-feedback momentum and energy budgets cease to explain gas loss or quiescence, and AGN-linked observables become necessary to reproduce the measured quenched fraction and baryon deficit.
active_papers.title: Locating the transition from stellar-feedback to AGN-feedback regulation

active_papers.source_text: The inferred frequency and impact of AGN outflows depend strongly on gas phase, and a common-denominator multiphase census will change which feedback conclusions are supportable.
active_papers.title: A multiphase, common-denominator census of AGN-driven outflows

active_papers.source_text: In quenched or transitioning galaxies, low star formation is driven primarily by reduced molecular-gas fraction in some regimes and by reduced star-formation efficiency in others.
active_papers.title: Distinguishing molecular-gas depletion from suppressed star-formation efficiency in quenched galaxies

active_papers.source_text: If subgrid feedback prescriptions are correct, forward-modelled mock observations from simulations should reproduce observed gas fractions, quenched fractions, outflow tracers, and morphology distributions under the same selection functions.
active_papers.title: Forward-modelled validation of cosmological feedback prescriptions
